title: Chinese Communist Revolution and founding of the People's Republic of China
summary: After the Nationalist-Communist civil war resumed in 1946, the People's Liberation Army won Manchuria, north China and the Yangtze line in 1948–49. Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China at Tiananmen on 1 October 1949; the Nationalist government withdrew to Taiwan in December.
card: Full-scale fighting between Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists and the Chinese Communist Party resumed in 1946 after the failed Marshall mediation, and three great campaigns in late 1948 and early 1949 broke the Nationalist armies. On 1 October 1949 Mao Zedong announced the People's Republic before a crowd of about 300,000 in Beijing, and by 10 December Chiang had flown from Chengdu to Taiwan, where about 1.2 million mainlanders had gathered. The new state's land reform redistributed land to some 300 million peasants and killed on the order of one to two million people, a toll that historians still debate.
what:
The Chinese Communist Revolution is the process by which the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and its People's Liberation Army (PLA) defeated the Nationalist (Kuomintang) government of the Republic of China on the mainland and founded the People's Republic of China (PRC) on 1 October 1949. After Japan's surrender in 1945 the two parties, which had fought each other before 1937, competed to take over territory, above all Manchuria. American general George Marshall brokered a ceasefire on 10 January 1946, but it collapsed and by summer 1946 the Nationalists were attacking in full force. Mao Zedong's own figures show the balance moving: the Nationalists had about 4.3 million men in July 1946 and the PLA about 1.2 million, but by November 1948 the PLA claimed more than 3 million against a Nationalist force of about 2.9 million.

The decisive blows came in three campaigns. In Manchuria the Liaoshen campaign ended with the fall of Shenyang on 2 November 1948, after a months-long siege of Changchun in which at least 160,000 civilians are said to have died. The Huaihai campaign around Xuzhou (6 November 1948 to 10 January 1949) and the Pingjin campaign (Tianjin taken on 14 January 1949; Beiping surrendered peacefully on 31 January) destroyed or absorbed the Nationalists' best formations, by PLA reckoning more than a million men. On 21 April 1949 the PLA crossed the Yangtze, took Nanjing two days later and Shanghai on 27 May. A Political Consultative Conference of Communists, minor parties and other groups met in September, and on 1 October Mao proclaimed the new government from the Tiananmen gate in Beijing. The Nationalist government withdrew from the mainland, last sitting in Chengdu; its Executive Yuan held its first meeting in Taipei on 9 December and Chiang Kai-shek flew there from Chengdu on 10 December.

Interpretations differ. Official PRC accounts describe a people's war of liberation against a corrupt, foreign-backed regime. American debate of the time asked who had lost China; later scholars emphasise Nationalist weakness, Communist organisation and the choices of both sides. Historians such as Frank Dikötter stress the terror that accompanied consolidation, including land reform killings estimated at 1.5 to 2 million.

uncertainty.note: The record spans the resumption of full-scale civil war (summer 1946, after the 10 January 1946 ceasefire collapsed) to the Nationalist leadership's departure from Chengdu for Taiwan on 10 December 1949. The proclamation of the PRC is a precise point inside the span: 1 October 1949, ceremony from 3 p.m. Beijing time (07:00 UTC). Sources I opened give no single day for the resumption of full-scale war; it is a process over spring and summer 1946. The end is taken as the Taiwan move, though the PLA continued to take southern and western provinces to the end of 1949 and Hainan and others in 1950.

how: The war was decided by shifting strength and by a small number of huge battles. Mao's own estimate in November 1948 was that the revolution would take about five years from July 1946, and that after the autumn victories only about one more year was needed. In Manchuria the Communists first isolated Changchun and starved it into surrender in October 1948, took Shenyang on 2 November. They then turned south: the Huaihai campaign (6 November 1948 to 10 January 1949) around Xuzhou destroyed, by PLA count, about 555,000 Nationalist troops; the Pingjin campaign encircled Fu Zuoyi's more than 600,000 men, took Tianjin by assault on 14 January and obtained the peaceful surrender of Beiping on 31 January. Peace talks failed in April 1949, and the order for a country-wide advance on 21 April sent the Second and Third Field Armies across the Yangtze on a front of more than 500 km. Nanjing fell on 23 April, Shanghai on 27 May. The CCP then convened a Political Consultative Conference in September that adopted a Common Programme and elected a government, announced on 1 October with Mao as chairman. Mao had declared in June that China must "lean to one side", toward the Soviet Union. In the same period the United States, which Mao said had backed Chiang with money, weapons and advisers rather than a large invasion, published a White Paper on 5 August explaining its policy.
why_it_matters: The revolution replaced a weak, fragmented republic with a centralised party-state that has governed mainland China ever since, and every later episode of PRC history (collectivisation, the Great Leap Forward, the Cultural Revolution, reform and opening) grew out of the institutions and leadership created in 1949. It also divided the Chinese world in two: about 1.2 million mainlanders reached Taiwan with the Nationalist government, which declared martial law there in May 1949, and the question of Taiwan's status remains a central flashpoint of East Asian security. The proclamation fixed China's place in the Cold War. Mao tied the new state to the Soviet Union, the United States split over who had lost China, and, as the U.S. Office of the Historian notes, the Korean War ended any chance of accommodation and led Washington to protect the Nationalist government on Taiwan. Inside China, land reform gave some 300 million landless peasants land by the Party's count, but it also killed an estimated one to two million people and taught villagers to take part in political violence, a legacy still discussed in the PRC and abroad. Had the Nationalists held the Yangtze line, or had Marshall's coalition scheme survived, none of this would have unfolded as it did: there would have been no PRC in 1949, no Sino-Soviet alliance of the 1950s, and a different Korean War. Mao himself had written in November 1948 that about one more year would be needed, so the victory came on roughly the timetable he expected only after the autumn campaigns had transformed the odds.

related.because: Mao stated that the October Revolution brought Marxism-Leninism to China, giving Chinese radicals the framework and model on which the CCP was founded in 1921.
Japan's defeat in 1945 removed the wartime reason for Nationalist-Communist cooperation and left both sides competing to take over Japanese-held territory.
The Soviet occupation of Manchuria left large stocks of captured Japanese weapons and a strategic base that helped the Communists, who had held no major cities, to build their northeastern army.
The U.S. Office of the Historian says the war ended any chance of an American accommodation with the new PRC and led Washington to adopt a policy of protecting the Nationalist government on Taiwan.

perspectives.holder: The CCP and the PRC state
perspectives.account: The war was a people's war of liberation in which the PLA, backed by the nation, defeated a reactionary Nationalist government allied with imperialism and established the sole legal government of China. Official histories present the Changchun siege as a decisive victory and do not mention the civilian deaths.

perspectives.holder: The Truman administration and the American "loss of China" debate
perspectives.account: The U.S. White Paper of August 1949 argued that only Chinese forces could decide the outcome; critics said the administration had lost China. Mao replied that American money and weapons had backed the Kuomintang and that U.S. prestige in China was bankrupt.

perspectives.holder: Historians stressing contingency and Communist strengths (as summarised by John W. Mackey)
perspectives.account: Mackey argues that the result reflected the ideologies, strategies and relative strength of the two parties rather than American conspiracy or incompetence, and that American power could not override conditions on the ground.

perspectives.holder: Frank Dikötter and historians of revolutionary violence
perspectives.account: The early years of the PRC were a period of systematic violence and calculated terror; land reform killed 1.5 to 2 million people, and the Party deliberately implicated villagers in the killing. Jeffrey Javed finds that the intensity of violence in land reform followed local government capacity to mobilise and control it rather than levels of inequality.

numbers.note: Frank Dikötter's estimate as reported by the University of Hong Kong. chineseposters.net gives "about one million" former landlords executed without attributing it; Javed describes estimates of "millions". No official count is available.

numbers.note: "At least 160,000", unattributed on the page; other estimates (150,000-300,000) exist but were not opened.

numbers.note: Including 582,086 Nationalist servicemen. Broader windows (1945-50) give about 2 million, not verified here.

numbers.label: Nationalist troops wiped out in the Huaihai campaign (PLA claim)
numbers.note: About 555,000 from 22 corps (56 divisions), including four divisions that went over. A claim by the winning side. Pingjin: Tianjin garrison over 130,000, campaign total over 520,000 (src-mao-pingjin).

numbers.label: People at the 1 October 1949 Tiananmen ceremony
numbers.note: "About 300,000 soldiers and civilians"; a PRC-friendly modern source.

audience_note: This record covers civil-war sieges and mass killing, including starvation of civilians in Changchun and the killing of landlords and others in land reform. Death figures are contested estimates; some come from the winning side's own claims.

importance.justification: The revolution created the People's Republic of China, ended the Chinese civil war on the mainland, split China from Taiwan and reshaped the Cold War in Asia.
